links_touching_record.rationale: Software requirement allocated from functional safety requirement

FB2-REV-000010 reviewed FB2-SW-SWR-000001 at revision 1 and enumerates it in reviewed_ids with the sha256 of the artifact's content at review time. Direction follows the pre-existing reviewed_by links in this registry, which run review -> artifact.

FB2-REV-000011 reviewed FB2-SW-SWR-000001 at revision 1 and enumerates it in reviewed_ids with the sha256 of the artifact's content at review time. Direction follows the pre-existing reviewed_by links in this registry, which run review -> artifact.

FB2-REV-000001 reviewed FB2-SW-SWR-000001 at revision 1 and enumerates it in reviewed_ids with the sha256 of the artifact's content at review time. Direction follows the pre-existing reviewed_by links in this registry, which run review -> artifact.

FB2-SW-IMP-000001 realises FB2-SW-SWR-000001 at the requirement level: the acquisition the statement calls for is triggered through AFE_StartMeasurement into the LTC sequencer, the PEC validation it calls for is LTC_CheckPec's per-LTC comparison, and the publication it calls for is the DATA_WRITE_DATA path. The requirement's own quantified figures - 20 Hz, 5 ms, 100% - are not established by this link, and the implementation record marks them as modelled rather than read from source.

FB2-SW-SWR-000001 is allocated to FB2-SW-DSN-000001 as the software requirement whose implementation that design details: the design's acquisition, PEC-validation and publication responsibilities are the requirement's own clauses. Direction is requirement -> design element, as master prompt section 13 declares for allocated_to.

FB2-SW-SWR-000001 requires 20 Hz acquisition, PEC/CRC validation before database write, and database publish within 5 ms. The specification's requirement_traceability entry records that one of those three - the PEC/CRC criterion - has an executed unit assertion, in the LTC 6813-1 PEC oracle group, and that the two timing criteria are neither asserted nor assertable in a harness that mocks the timebase and the SPI/DMA transfer. The verification_state recorded is partially_verified_at_unit_level. A verifies link is recorded because the specification does address the requirement and states what it does and does not reach; it is not recorded as evidence that the requirement is met.

asil_allocation_scope.classification_belongs_to: the hypothetical reference project declared by the synthetic_reference profile of this corpus
asil_allocation_scope.origin_field_relationship: Because this record now carries a back-inferred classification alongside its source-derived content, origin is 'derived' rather than 'source_observed': master prompt section 5 requires that an artefact containing both observed and modelled content must not be labelled wholly observed. Where this record's origin was 'source_observed' it has been changed to 'derived' for that reason and for no other; no statement, acceptance criterion, threshold, assumption, safety goal reference or mitigation text was altered in the same edit.
asil_allocation_scope.reading_rule: Any view, report or export that renders this record's asil value must render this field with it. An asil value shown without this field is a defect in that view, not a permissible abbreviation.
asil_allocation_scope.statement: The asil value in this record's safety_allocation is a RECONSTRUCTED value, not an observation and not a determination. It was produced by reading back the safety-goal classification of the hypothetical reference project this corpus also declares in its synthetic_reference profile, and by attributing that classification to this record because this corpus's own requirement set was written downstream of it. The real foxBMS 2 product has never had a hazard analysis and risk assessment. No HARA has been performed for it, none is claimed here, and nothing in this record may be read as one, as a partial one, or as a substitute for one.
what_this_field_asserts: That the recorded asil value equals the classification the reference project's safety concept and goal chain assigns to this element, as those records state it.
That the classification originates in the reference project and nowhere else.
That no classification has been performed for the real product by this corpus or by anyone on its behalf.
what_this_field_does_not_assert: It does not assert an ASIL for the real foxBMS 2 product. The real product's safety integrity level is undetermined, not ASIL_D; undetermined is the honest answer and this corpus has no standing to change it.
It does not assert that a hazard analysis and risk assessment exists for the real product in any form, complete or partial.

It does not assert that any design, in either profile, meets this ASIL. An allocation creates an obligation downstream; it is not evidence the obligation is discharged, and no execution record in this corpus discharges it for this element.
It does not assert ISO 26262 conformity, certification, or qualification of any product, supplier, tool or process.
It does not assert an Automotive SPICE capability level for any organisation.

It does not assert that the exposure or severity inputs behind the reference project's classification are evidenced. They are authored: the reference project's safety goal FB2-SAF-SGO-000001 already records that its exposure rating is an unevidenced authored input and that a single exposure step would move the whole classification one class lower.
asil_allocation_scope.why_the_value_is_still_here: The ASIL is retained rather than deleted because it is legitimate inside the fictional project: the reference project needs an allocated class at this element for its own argument to be internally consistent, and removing the number would leave the reference project's allocation silently unallocated. What was illegitimate was its presentation here, as an unqualified field on an as_is record that a reader could take as a statement about the product. That presentation is what this field removes.

revision_history.description: Added asil_allocation_scope, and moved the origin field from source_observed to derived. An independent audit flagged this record as asserting an unqualified ASIL on an as_is profile record, which presents a classification belonging to the hypothetical reference project as though it were a determination about the real foxBMS product. The ASIL value itself is untouched and remains ASIL_D, because it is legitimate inside the fictional project; what is different now is that the value can no longer be read without the reconstruction stated alongside it. It was previously source_observed.

shape_note: Deliberately not shaped like a corpus record: no top-level id, profile, artifact_type or source_refs, so that generating packets cannot change any coverage number. See the module docstring of make_review_packets.py.

signature_block._recording: Transcribe a completed signature into the record as human_approval_status plus a revision_history entry naming the reviewer, and archive the signed packet outside docs/artifacts/reviews/packets/.
signature_block._rule: Empty by construction. No automated process may fill this. Filling it in is the only thing that changes human_approval_status on the record, and the corpus rule `human_approval_rejected` fails validation on any record whose human_approval_status is not pending, so no tool can manufacture the state.

signature_policy: The signature block below is empty by construction. This tool has no code path that writes a decision, an approval, a signature or an execution verdict. Filling it is a human action.
